coverageDimensions:
SERVICE coverage would mean: of all AWS services that exist, for how many does AWS Config record at least one resource type. The page gives you nothing here. It never names a service, has no service column and no service list. You can derive 155 distinct AWS:: namespaces from the row prefixes, but that is your inference, not the page's claim, and a namespace is not a service: ApiGateway and ApiGatewayV2 are one service, ACMPCA is AWS Private CA, ElasticLoadBalancing and ElasticLoadBalancingV2 are one service. There is also no denominator — the page never says how many AWS services exist or which are out of scope. Treat service coverage as NOT SUPPLIED and refuse to compute a percentage from the prefixes.

REGION coverage would mean: of all AWS Regions, in how many is the capability offered. The page gives you the numerator only, and only implicitly: 38 named Regions appear as column headers, and each has at least one Yes, so Config records something in all 38. It never states that these 38 are every Region where AWS Config is available, never lists a Region as wholly unsupported, and gives no total Region count. So you get a 38-Region enumeration you may report as a list, but no honest ratio. The real per-Region number this page supports is not "is Config here" but "how much of the 558 does this Region get" — for example US West (Oregon) 538/558, Canada West (Calgary) 187/558, Asia Pacific (Taipei) 89/558, AWS GovCloud (US-West) 326/558.

RESOURCE TYPE coverage would mean: of all AWS resource types that exist, how many does AWS Config record, and where. This is the one dimension the page actually supplies, and it supplies it fully at cell granularity: 558 types x 38 Regions, 18,606 explicit Yes/No verdicts, 2,598 pairs unstated. The numerator is solid. The denominator is not on this page — AWS never says how many resource types exist in total (the CloudFormation registry is far larger than 558), so "AWS Config covers 558 resource types" is reportable but "AWS Config covers N% of resource types" is not, unless the denominator comes from a different source you name.

features.featureName: Resource Coverage by Region Availability (AWS Config resource type recording)
features.reasoning: The row label is the thing the capability reaches and it is enumerable: a CloudFormation-style resource type belonging to some other AWS service. Config recording it or not is a genuine coverage claim in both directions, and the page makes it in both directions with a Yes/No column. The axis is external: AWS::EC2::Instance exists whether or not AWS Config ever records it, so the ratio 13,383/18,606 or 385/558 is meaningful rather than true by construction. This is ONE capability, not six. The six H2 headings are a width-driven split of a single matrix — same header cell ("Resource type"), same Yes/No vocabulary, same semantics — and the union of the six row sets is exactly the 558 rows of the Americas table, which is a strict superset of every other table. Columns are values on the second dimension (Regions), not separate capabilities, so this is not a capabilities-across-the-top matrix and must not be split into 38 features either.
features.scope: Per Region. 38 Regions, named in the column headers of six geographically partitioned tables: North and South America 8 (US West N. California, US East N. Virginia, US West Oregon, US East Ohio, Canada West Calgary, Canada Central, Mexico Central, South America Sao Paulo), Europe 8 (Ireland, Frankfurt, London, Paris, Stockholm, Milan, Spain, Zurich), Asia Pacific 14 (Hong Kong, Taipei, Tokyo, Seoul, Osaka, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Singapore, Sydney, Jakarta, Melbourne, Malaysia, New Zealand, Thailand), China 2 (Beijing, Ningxia), Africa and Middle East 4 (Cape Town, Tel Aviv, Bahrain, UAE), GovCloud 2 (US-West, US-East). The unit of truth is the (resourceType, Region) cell, not the row.
features.statuses: Every cell is explicitly Yes or No; there are no blanks, no footnotes, no notes, no retired or deprecated markers anywhere on the page (grep for note/Note/retired/deprecated returns only NotebookInstance strings). Status is carried by an icon plus the literal word: success_icon.png + "Yes", negative_icon.png + "No". Stated totals: 18,606 cells = 13,383 Yes + 5,223 No (verified, they sum exactly). Per section: Americas 3,191 Yes / 1,273 No over 558 rows x 8; Europe 3,158 / 946 over 513 x 8; Asia Pacific 4,595 / 2,573 over 512 x 14; China 559 / 35 over 297 x 2; Africa and Middle East 1,276 / 340 over 404 x 4; GovCloud 604 / 56 over 330 x 2. A third status exists but is never written down: the tables carry different row counts (558, 513, 512, 297, 404, 330), so 2,598 of the 558 x 38 = 21,204 possible pairs are UNSTATED — the resource type is simply absent from that geography's table. Unstated is not No and must be recorded as a separate state. All 558 types are Yes in at least one Region (zero all-No rows); 248 types appear in all six tables; 67 are Yes in every Region in which they are listed. Every row label matches ^AWS::[A-Za-z0-9]+::[A-Za-z0-9]+$ with no exceptions.

shouldNotExtract: The six H2 headings (North and South America Regions, Europe Regions, Asia Pacific Regions, China Regions, Africa and Middle East Regions, GovCloud Regions) — they are page furniture and geographic grouping labels, never capabilities and never axis values; the real Region names live only in the column headers. The `` HTML anchors after each heading. The `| --- |` separator rows and the `**Resource type**` header cell. The success_icon.png / negative_icon.png image URLs inside every cell — they are the Yes/No glyph, so strip the markdown image and keep only the word, and never let an image URL become a value. The whole "## See also" section and its single bullet, which is the AWS boilerplate about optional skills for AI coding assistants and the `aws agent-toolkit search-skills --search-query config` command — that is a CLI suggestion, not coverage. There are no quotas, prices, prerequisites, code examples or troubleshooting on this page to reject.
trap:
Two, and both produce confident wrong numbers.

First and worst: computing per-Region coverage against the local table's row count instead of the 558-type union. The tables are region-partitioned with unequal row counts, so China (Beijing) reads 292 Yes of 297 rows = 98% and AWS GovCloud (US-West) reads 326 of 330 = 99%, while US West (N. California) reads 385 of 558 = 69%. The map then declares Beijing better covered than N. California. The truth is the reverse: against the correct 558 denominator, Beijing is 292/558 = 52% and N. California is 385/558 = 69%. Absence of a resource type from a partition table is a third state (unstated, 2,598 pairs), not Yes, and not No either — it must be stored as its own value.

Second: treating the six H2 sections as six capabilities and emitting six features with six separate percentages, or emitting the 38 Region columns as 38 capabilities. Both destroy the matrix. It is one capability with a resourceType axis and a per-Region second dimension.

Two smaller ones. The page is 1.8 MB and a naive fetch truncates: a summarizing fetch of this exact URL returned "one H2 heading, one table, 8 Regions" and claimed that was the whole page — a parser that trusts it silently loses 30 Regions and 5 tables. And deriving a service list from the AWS:: prefix and presenting 155 as "services covered" invents a claim the page never makes.
whatThePageStates: This page states which resource types AWS Config supports in each AWS Region. It contains no prose at all: after the H1 there are six H2 sections (North and South America, Europe, Asia Pacific, China, Africa and Middle East, GovCloud) and each holds exactly one table whose rows are resource types in AWS::Service::Type form and whose columns are named Regions, with every cell a green-tick "Yes" or a red-cross "No". Counted by hand off the page: 558 distinct resource types, 38 Regions, 18,606 stated Yes/No cells (13,383 Yes, 5,223 No), 155 distinct AWS:: service namespaces derivable from the row labels. The six sections are a geographic split of one table, not six capabilities.
